entry.subject: U.S.-priority external experimental-validation routing after RUN-008 physical boundary
entry.trigger: The originator cannot physically build the JANUS Engine article; identify laboratories and U.S. government research pathways capable of independent review and hardware validation.
result: The highest-priority U.S. route is ONR Global because its mission explicitly includes connecting international scientists to the U.S. Naval Research and Development Establishment and supporting international research relevant to naval S&T.

NUWC Newport / Northeast Tech Bridge is a very high-fit transition route because its focus includes autonomous and robotic undersea vehicles, marine materials and bio-inspired science and engineering.

WHOI Oceanographic Systems Laboratory / Applied Ocean Physics & Engineering is a very high-fit independent laboratory target because it physically designs and builds AUV systems for science and defense.
NRL Alternative Energy / Technology Transfer is a high-fit U.S. Navy laboratory route for fuel cells, batteries, hydrogen storage, harvesting and power systems.
DARPA STO/MXO remains a high-risk/high-reward route through a current office-wide BAA rather than an undirected unsolicited proposal.
DIU is deprioritized until a physical prototype or matching solicitation exists; its current open-solicitation page lists no openings and its normal process favors commercially viable technology.
ARPA-E is secondary unless a U.S. prime partner and applicable NOFO are identified because U.S.-performance and applicant restrictions can apply.
entry.decision: Prepare a concise nonconfidential U.S.-style technical brief centered on the exact R0P1A experiment and the deliberately unresolved RUN-008 measurements. Contact targets sequentially and maintain a recipient ledger so the same organization is not contacted twice accidentally.
